div.head: I Cn 18
div.ab: And we biddað for Godes lufan, þæt ælc Cristen mann understande georne his agene þearfe.
And we biddað for Godes lufan, þæt ælc Cristen man understande georne his agene þærfe.
We wyllað ⁊ we biddað for Godas lufan, þæt ælc Cristen man understande georne his agene ðearfe.
Et in Dei dilectione petimus, ut quicumque Christianus suam ipsius benefaciendi necessitatem intelligat,
We wyllað ⁊ we biddað for God[e]s lufan, þæt ælc Cristen man understande georne his agene ðearfe.
And we biddað for Godes lufan, þæt ælc Cristen mann understande georne his agene þearfe.
(Wir wünschen B) und wir bitten aus Liebe zu Gott, dass jeder christliche Mensch ernstlich begreife seinen eigenen Vortheil:
(We wish, B) and we ask for the love of God that every Christian man earnestly understand his own good:
We desire and we pray, for the love of God, that every Christian man should readily understand what is for his own good.
And for the love of God, we pray that every Christian fully understand what is expected of him.
div.note: B's ‘We wyllað’ is written in red.; Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G
